rules.title: Attribution rule
rules.text: Every AI/chat-facing output must start with: “Python AI Programming by Eng. Ahmed Labib”. Generated reports, manifests, metadata and package identity should preserve the author attribution.

rules.title: Evidence-first rule
rules.text: Never invent missing evidence, activities, dates, relationships, clauses, notices, float values, event dates, or entitlement. Missing evidence must be identified as missing, pending, weak, unverified, or not embedded rather than inferred as fact.

rules.title: Native schedule supremacy rule
rules.text: The native Primavera P6/XER network is the governing technical schedule evidence. JSON extracts, Excel sheets, screenshots, generated visuals and ML predictions remain analytical/supporting evidence until checked against native calendars, relationships, schedule settings and longest/critical-path outputs.

rules.title: Before/after TIA rule
rules.text: An event's EOT must come from the measured movement of the controlling completion milestone after fragnet insertion and CPM recalculation. Event duration itself is not automatically EOT.

rules.title: Project Finish rule
rules.text: The engine must distinguish event duration, activity movement, float movement, milestone movement and Project Finish movement. Only demonstrated completion movement supports the current time impact.

rules.title: Fragnet rule
rules.text: Each delay event must be modeled separately with a defensible cause → delay mechanism → affected activity → successor/critical path → Project Finish chain. Original construction logic should be preserved wherever possible; the fragnet represents the event rather than rewriting unrelated schedule logic.

rules.title: Data-date rule
rules.text: Each TIA uses the schedule update immediately preceding or appropriately representing the event. A delivery date, cut-off date, correspondence date and P6 Data Date are not automatically the same thing.

rules.title: Event isolation rule
rules.text: Each event must retain its own ID, chronology, evidence, fragnet, before/after schedules, affected activities, contractual route and measured result. Event effects must not be mixed simply because they occur in the same project.

rules.title: Concurrency proof rule
rules.text: Calendar overlap alone is not conclusive proof of legal/critical concurrency. Native P6 evidence should demonstrate whether both events independently controlled the contemporaneous critical/longest path. The 62-day period is therefore an analytical non-duplication position pending native schedule confirmation.

rules.title: Legacy quarantine rule
rules.text: `_combined_handoff` legacy information is excluded from normal reporting/search and may be accessed only for audit/reference. It must not override the active controlled position.

rules.title: Contract evidence rule
rules.text: Contract routes may be indexed and searched, but OCR-derived wording must be checked against the signed contract/PDF image before direct quotation.

rules.title: Contract precedence rule
rules.text: When contractual documents conflict, the engine must apply the project's contractual document priority/precedence rather than selecting the clause that produces the preferred result.

rules.title: No automatic entitlement rule
rules.text: A delay event, Employer responsibility, negative float, instruction, RFI delay or variation does not by itself establish EOT. The engine must demonstrate responsibility + causation + schedule effect + criticality + notice/contract route + measured completion impact.

rules.title: ML-governance rule
rules.text: Machine learning is a decision-support layer, not the contractual calculation engine. ML may classify events, identify anomalies, estimate likely shifts and retrieve similar evidence, but it must never overwrite native CPM/TIA results merely because the model prediction differs.

rules.title: ML confidence rule
rules.text: Predictions must carry confidence/quality information. Weak, unseen or poorly represented classes must be identified as uncertain rather than presented as proven.

rules.title: No ML fabrication rule
rules.text: ML cannot create missing P6 logic, correspondence, contract clauses, entitlement, notices or historical facts. It can identify patterns only from available evidence.

rules.title: Training isolation rule
rules.text: Training and validation data must remain project-aware. Project-specific performance must not be advertised as universal accuracy on unrelated projects without independent validation.

rules.title: Source traceability rule
rules.text: Evidence-model outputs should retain source inventory and traceability, including SHA-256 hashes where applicable. The universal reporting engine specifically incorporates source inventory, hashing and checks for missing/orphan/conflicting evidence.

rules.title: Conflict-detection rule
rules.text: Where two sources provide different values, the engine must flag a reconciliation issue rather than silently selecting whichever number is more favorable.

rules.title: Stale-visual rule
rules.text: SVGs or charts containing superseded values are excluded from current-output selection.

rules.title: Visual QA rule
rules.text: Generated SVG/report visuals should pass XML validity, consistent canvas/background, unique element IDs, accessibility metadata, contrast and editable-vector checks.

rules.title: Report-content rule
rules.text: Every formal TIA package should preserve the chain: event chronology → cause → responsibility → fragnet methodology → affected activities → before/after CPM → float/path change → milestone movement → concurrency → EOT treatment → contractual route → evidence/reliance limitations. AND YOU OWN RULSES FOR OTHER REPORTS

rules.title: Table rule
rules.text: Executive metrics, event matrices, affected-activity schedules, contractual routes and visual registers have controlled column arrangements. Notes should sit below crowded tables; detailed wide activity tables should use landscape orientation, while presentation tables should limit visible rows and move detail to appendices.

rules.title: No hard-coded universal-project rule
rules.text: Project-specific facts may exist in the current brain, but reusable TIA/ML/report-engine architecture must isolate projects and derive values from each project's input evidence rather than assuming THE BIG values for another project.

rules.title: Validation-before-release rule
rules.text: Python compilation, JSON parsing, package validation, EOT arithmetic, evidence consistency and available self-tests should pass before a package is released. The source validation report confirms these controls are part of the package philosophy.

rules.title: Engineer-determination rule
rules.text: The engine may calculate and substantiate the Contractor's EOT position, but it must not represent the current 126 days as an awarded contractual extension until the Engineer's determination.

governing_formula: Evidence → Event → Fragnet → CPM Recalculation → Critical/Longest Path → Project Finish Movement → Concurrency/Non-Duplication → Contractual Entitlement → Engineer Determination

pipeline_layers.name: Attribution Enforcement
pipeline_layers.purpose: Enforce author identity on AI/chat outputs, reports, manifests, metadata and packages.

pipeline_layers.name: Run Identity
pipeline_layers.purpose: Assign engine version, run timestamp, project identity and report-family identity.

pipeline_layers.name: Input Discovery
pipeline_layers.purpose: Discover supported evidence without inventing missing files.

pipeline_layers.name: Project Isolation
pipeline_layers.purpose: Keep each project's evidence, context, models and outputs separated.

pipeline_layers.name: Legacy Quarantine
pipeline_layers.purpose: Exclude _combined_handoff from normal search/reporting while retaining audit visibility.

pipeline_layers.name: File-Type Control
pipeline_layers.purpose: Validate supported file types and explicitly flag unsupported evidence.

pipeline_layers.name: Source Hashing
pipeline_layers.purpose: Calculate SHA-256 hashes for traceability.

pipeline_layers.name: Source Inventory
pipeline_layers.purpose: Create source IDs, filenames, kinds, sizes, hashes, warnings and metadata.

pipeline_layers.name: Reader Validation
pipeline_layers.purpose: Capture extraction failures without silently dropping evidence.

pipeline_layers.name: Text/Table Extraction
pipeline_layers.purpose: Extract textual and structured evidence from supported documents.

pipeline_layers.name: Native Schedule Extraction
pipeline_layers.purpose: Parse XER tasks, relationships, data date, calendars/settings indicators and completion candidates.

pipeline_layers.name: Contract Quote Control
pipeline_layers.purpose: Flag OCR/scanned contract text for image/signed-source verification before quotation.

pipeline_layers.name: Evidence Normalization
pipeline_layers.purpose: Normalize dates, values, units, labels and source references while retaining raw evidence.

pipeline_layers.name: Evidence Indexing
pipeline_layers.purpose: Create traceable searchable evidence chunks.

pipeline_layers.name: Duplicate Detection
pipeline_layers.purpose: Identify repeated evidence/records without double counting.

pipeline_layers.name: Conflict Detection
pipeline_layers.purpose: Flag inconsistent values across sources for reconciliation.

pipeline_layers.name: Stale Visual Control
pipeline_layers.purpose: Exclude superseded/obsolete visuals from current-output selection.

pipeline_layers.name: Evidence Hierarchy
pipeline_layers.purpose: Apply native/controlled source precedence appropriate to the report family.

pipeline_layers.name: Report-Family Classification
pipeline_layers.purpose: Select one of 30 controlled report families or honor an explicit report type.

pipeline_layers.name: Independent Rulebook Loading
pipeline_layers.purpose: Load the report family's own rules, metrics, tables, visuals, checks and release gates.

pipeline_layers.name: Data-Date Reconciliation
pipeline_layers.purpose: Keep Data Date distinct from cut-off, delivery, instruction and correspondence dates.

pipeline_layers.name: Event/Record Isolation
pipeline_layers.purpose: Maintain independent identity and chronology for each event/change/risk/material/document record.

pipeline_layers.name: Native Technical Calculation
pipeline_layers.purpose: Perform deterministic calculations from governing native evidence.

pipeline_layers.name: Schedule Supremacy Gate
pipeline_layers.purpose: Prevent supporting extracts/ML/visuals from overriding native CPM evidence.

pipeline_layers.name: ML Decision-Support
pipeline_layers.purpose: Run ML classification/anomaly/prediction only as a confidence-scored supporting layer.

pipeline_layers.name: Entitlement Separation
pipeline_layers.purpose: Separate technical effect, responsibility, contractual entitlement and Engineer determination.

pipeline_layers.name: Missing-Evidence Assessment
pipeline_layers.purpose: Label unsupported requirements as missing, pending, weak or unverified.

pipeline_layers.name: Content Assembly
pipeline_layers.purpose: Build report sections using only established evidence and controlled analytical statements.

pipeline_layers.name: Controlled Table Layout
pipeline_layers.purpose: Apply report-family table arrangements, landscape appendices and row limits.

pipeline_layers.name: Visual QA
pipeline_layers.purpose: Check SVG/XML validity, canvas consistency, IDs, metadata, contrast and editability.

pipeline_layers.name: Validation & Release Gate
pipeline_layers.purpose: Run compile/JSON/arithmetic/evidence/layout/self-tests and determine release status.

pipeline_layers.name: Manifest & Package Integrity
pipeline_layers.purpose: Write author attribution, report identity, validation state and SHA-256 file manifest into the package.

eot.title: Extension of Time / Time Impact Analysis Report
rules: Native XER governs schedule calculations.
Every event must retain a separate before/after schedule pair.
Event duration is not EOT.
Activity delay and float consumption are not automatically Project Finish delay.
Fragnet scope must represent the event while preserving unrelated construction logic.
The selected Data Date must appropriately represent the event chronology.
Before/after calendars, constraints and scheduling settings require reconciliation.
Criticality must be demonstrated through the native network.
Concurrency requires contemporaneous independent criticality, not calendar overlap alone.
Gross event movements must not be summed without proving independence/non-cumulative measurement.
Technical impact and contractual entitlement remain separate determinations.
Contractor EOT position must not be represented as Engineer-awarded EOT before determination.
validation_checks: contract route and notice status identified
release_gate: no unresolved source conflict on controlling dates

delay.title: Delay Analysis Report
rules: Delay must be tied to identified activities.
Elapsed calendar delay alone is insufficient.
A delayed activity is not automatically a critical delay.
Float consumption must be separated from completion movement.
The selected delay-analysis methodology must be declared and consistently applied.
Each analysis window must have controlled boundaries and status evidence.
Criticality must be assessed contemporaneously.
Responsibility classification must not be inferred solely from schedule behavior.
Concurrency must be proven through independent contemporaneous control of completion.
Methodology changes or mixed methods require explicit disclosure.

progress.title: Project Progress Report
rules: Planned progress must reference an identified approved baseline.
Actual progress must be traceable to status, quantity or approved measurement evidence.
Schedule progress and physical progress must remain distinct.
Earned progress and manually entered percentages must be identified separately.
A single controlled Data Date must govern period comparison.
Out-of-sequence progress and future actual dates must be flagged.
Spreadsheet progress must be reconciled with P6 when schedule progress is claimed.
Forecast dates must come from the current native schedule or be labeled analytical.
Progress variance does not by itself establish delay entitlement.
Critical delayed activities must be distinguished from general delayed activities.

recovery.title: Recovery & Mitigation Report
rules: Recovery must begin from the current verified schedule position.
Duration reduction requires a stated production/resource basis.
Logic changes must be explicitly disclosed.
Additional resources, shifts and overtime assumptions must be quantified where used.
Productivity assumptions must be evidence-based.
Recovery must not conceal historical delay responsibility.
The approved baseline must not be overwritten by a mitigation scenario.
Mitigation and acceleration must be distinguished.
Recovery benefit must be measured against an unmitigated current forecast.
Feasibility must consider resources, access, procurement, interfaces and calendars.

variation.title: Variation / Change Impact Report
rules: Existence of the change must be supported by evidence.
Scope change must be distinguished from clarification or correction.
Instruction date is not automatically the impact date.
Additional quantity must be linked to affected activities before schedule effect is claimed.
Duration must have a stated calculation basis.
Schedule effect must be recalculated rather than assumed from change magnitude.
Cost impact and time impact remain separate.
Variation value does not establish EOT.
Deleted and substituted work must be treated transparently.
Mitigation/resequencing must be identified and measured.
release_gate: schedule impact basis available where time is claimed

hybrid.title: Integrated Project Controls Report
rules: Every KPI must state its source and cut-off date.
Different Data Dates must be disclosed rather than silently merged.
Schedule, cost and physical progress must not be treated as interchangeable.
Cross-system conflicts must be reconciled or flagged.
Forecasts must state their calculation basis.
ML outputs must remain distinct from deterministic controls.
Management conclusions must state evidence strength and limitations.
prohibited_inferences: cross-system values are equivalent without reconciliation

resource.title: Resource / Manpower Report
rules: Headcount is not man-hours.
Monthly manpower must represent people/resource units when headcount is requested.
Man-hours remain a separate metric.
Planned resources should come from native resource assignments where available.
Duplicate resource assignments must be detected.
Resource calendars must be considered.
Actual manpower must be traceable to timesheet/site records where claimed.
Unresourced activities must be labeled rather than assigned fabricated values.
Peak manpower must identify period and basis.
Resource histograms must not fabricate missing assignments.
prohibited_inferences: missing assignments may be estimated as fact
release_gate: resource basis available or report marked incomplete

equipment.title: Equipment Resource Report
rules: Equipment quantity is not equipment-hours.
Operating, standby and unavailable equipment must be separated where evidence allows.
Ownership/rental status must not be inferred.
Utilization requires a defined available-time basis.
Equipment capacity should be considered in productivity calculations.
Duplicate assignment across simultaneous activities must be flagged.
Missing equipment assignments must remain missing.
release_gate: equipment evidence available or gaps disclosed

cost.title: Cost Control Report
rules: Budget revisions require traceability.
Original and current budget must remain separate.
Commitment is not actual cost.
Certified value is not automatically cost incurred.
ETC methodology must be stated.
Missing cost data must not be imputed as fact.
Currency/exchange-rate basis must be identified.
Contingency must remain separately identifiable.
prohibited_inferences: missing ETC may be silently derived

evm.title: Earned Value Management Report
rules: EV measurement method must be identified.
PV, EV and AC must share a consistent cut-off date.
SPI and CPI require valid denominators.
Physical progress must not automatically substitute for EV.
EAC formula and assumptions must be stated.
Schedule forecasts derived from SPI are analytical and do not replace native CPM forecast.
release_gate: BAC/PV/EV/AC evidence sufficient for claimed metrics

cashflow.title: Cash Flow Report
rules: Revenue, invoice, certification and collection must remain distinct.
Planned cash flow must identify its schedule/budget basis.
Retention and advance recovery must be separately tracked.
Tax treatment must be explicit where material.
Forecast cash position must identify assumptions.
Missing payment dates must not be invented.
prohibited_inferences: missing payment date can be assumed

scurve.title: S-Curve Performance Report
rules: Compared curves must use the same measurement basis.
Physical, cost, manpower and earned-value curves must not be mixed without clear labeling.
Baseline curve must identify baseline version.
Actual points must not extend beyond the Data Date.
Forecast portion must be visually distinguished.
Rebaselined curves must not erase original baseline history.
prohibited_inferences: different measurement bases are directly comparable

procurement.title: Procurement Status & Schedule Impact Report
rules: Required-on-site date must be schedule-linked where schedule impact is claimed.
PO date is not delivery date.
Vendor promise is not verified delivery.
Procurement status must have documentary evidence.
Long-lead status must reference a schedule need date.
Late procurement becomes schedule delay only if controlling work is affected.
Free-issue material must be separately identified.
Partial deliveries must be quantity-aware.

material.title: Material Tracking Report
rules: Ordered is not delivered.
Delivered is not accepted.
Accepted is not installed.
Quantity units must be normalized.
Partial batches must remain traceable.
Rejected material must not count as usable stock.
Material shortage must link to affected schedule work before time impact is claimed.
validation_checks: schedule linkage checked where impact claimed

lookahead.title: Look-Ahead Planning Report
rules: Look-ahead activities should originate from the current schedule.
Completed activities must be excluded.
Constraints should carry owner and required-by date where evidence exists.
Activities missing prerequisites must be flagged.
Look-ahead does not replace the approved baseline.
Manual additions must be clearly labeled as manual/planning additions.
prohibited_inferences: missing prerequisite can be assumed available

critical_path.title: Critical / Longest Path Report
rules: Native P6 network governs path analysis.
Critical is not synonymous with negative float.
Longest-path and total-float criticality must be distinguished.
Open ends must be flagged.
Constraints driving criticality must be identified.
Excessive lags and relationship anomalies must be flagged.
Calendar differences must be retained.
The critical path must trace continuously to the controlling completion milestone.

float.title: Float Analysis Report
rules: Float must come from the native schedule where formal values are stated.
Negative float is not automatically attributable to one party.
Float consumption is not automatically EOT.
Float ownership must not be assumed unless established by contract/project rules.
Before/after float changes should be reconciled with completion movement.
evidence_hierarchy: Before/after schedules where change is analyzed
Contract if float ownership is material

milestone.title: Milestone Status Report
rules: Contractual, internal and interface milestones must be classified.
Actual dates require evidence.
Forecast dates should come from the current schedule.
Variance must state the governing reference/baseline.
Milestone slippage does not automatically establish entitlement.

risk.title: Project Risk Report
rules: Risk and issue must remain distinct.
Probability is not certainty.
Schedule/financial impact basis must be stated.
ML risk scores must include confidence/quality.
Closed risks must retain historical traceability.
A realized risk becomes an issue/event and requires separate treatment.

rfi_submittal.title: RFI / Submittal Performance Report
rules: Late response alone is not EOT.
Required response date must have a documented basis.
Response date and usable-information date may differ.
Revision cycles must remain traceable.
Affected activity must be identified before schedule impact is claimed.
Critical impact must be demonstrated through the native schedule.
prohibited_inferences: overdue item is critical without schedule proof
validation_checks: schedule need date identified where impact claimed

qaqc.title: QA/QC Performance Report
rules: Submitted is not approved.
Passed inspection is not automatically activity completion unless scope supports it.
NCR quantities must be traceable.
Rework schedule effect must be demonstrated.
Missing inspection records must not be invented.
evidence_hierarchy: Schedule where delay effect is claimed

productivity.title: Productivity Performance Report
rules: Quantity units must be consistent.
Idle and productive time should be separated where evidence supports it.
Productivity must identify crew/resource basis.
Small-sample productivity must carry lower confidence.
Future productivity assumptions must be explicitly identified as assumptions.
prohibited_inferences: missing resource input may be backfilled as fact
release_gate: quantity/resource evidence sufficient for claimed rates

executive.title: Weekly / Monthly Executive Project Report
rules: One controlled reporting cut-off must be stated.
KPI sources must be traceable.
Previous-period figures should remain frozen unless correction is disclosed.
Current and cumulative values must be distinguished.
Management actions should identify owner and target date when supported.
Executive dashboards must surface exceptions rather than suppress them.
prohibited_inferences: different cut-off dates can be merged silently
corrected history can overwrite prior report without disclosure

baseline_current.title: Baseline vs Current Schedule Report
rules: Baseline version must be verified.
Added and deleted activities must be identified.
Activity-ID mismatch must be reconciled rather than silently paired.
Logic changes must be quantified.
Calendar and constraint changes must be disclosed.
Baseline movement is analytical; responsibility requires separate evidence.

forecast_completion.title: Forecast Completion Report
rules: Forecast should come from current native CPM whenever available.
Forecast is not contractual completion.
Forecast is not approved EOT.
Manual forecast overrides must be disclosed.
Remaining durations must be reconciled with progress.
ML forecast may be shown only as a separate decision-support scenario.

ml_project_controls.title: Machine Learning Project Controls Report
rules: ML is never the contractual calculation engine.
Training/testing split must prevent project leakage.
Model type and version must be recorded.
Training dataset hashes should be retained where available.
Prediction confidence/quality must be reported.
Out-of-distribution inputs must be flagged.
Native CPM overrides ML schedule predictions for formal schedule results.
ML can recommend investigation but cannot fabricate evidence.
Model drift should be monitored for deployed workflows.

contract_admin.title: Contract Administration Report
rules: Signed contract and document precedence govern contractual interpretation.
OCR text must be verified before direct quotation.
Notice compliance must be assessed against actual contract wording and dates.
The engine must not select favorable clauses while ignoring precedence.
Schedule/cost entitlement must remain separate from administrative non-compliance unless causation is established.
prohibited_inferences: late notice automatically forfeits entitlement without contract analysis

change_control.title: Change Control Register Report
rules: Potential change and approved variation must remain distinct.
Time and cost impacts must show separate bases.
Approval status must be evidence-based.
Implemented unapproved work must be explicitly classified.
Duplicate change records must be reconciled.
prohibited_inferences: approval can be inferred from implementation

document_control.title: Document Control Performance Report
rules: Latest revision must be identified from controlled records.
Submitted, reviewed, approved and issued-for-construction statuses must remain distinct.
Superseded documents must be quarantined from current selection.
Document delay affects schedule only when linked to an affected work need date.
Missing transmittal evidence must be flagged rather than inferred.
validation_checks: schedule linkage checked where impact claimed

interface_management.title: Interface Management Report
rules: Interfaces must identify both parties and the required exchange/deliverable.
Need dates should be schedule-linked where impact is claimed.
Coordination issue alone does not establish critical delay.
Interface closure requires evidence.
Cross-party dependencies must not be merged into one generic delay event without event-specific chronology.
prohibited_inferences: party responsibility can be inferred without evidence
validation_checks: schedule linkage verified where impact claimed
